text_blocks.snippet: Common Active Scams in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Government & Law Enforcement Impersonation: Scammers pose as the U.S. Attorney’s Office , local sheriff's offices (such as and Sangamon counties), or municipal police departments. They claim victims have missed court, face active warrants, or need to pay for GPS ankle monitors, demanding immediate payment over the phone.

DMV & Utility Phishing Texts: Fraudulent text messages mimicking the Illinois DMV/Secretary of State or I-Pass/Illinois Tollway claim that license statuses are expiring or tolls are unpaid, pushing users to click malicious phishing links .

Online Shopping & Fake Tariffs: Fake retail sites advertised on social media offer steep discounts, then follow up post-purchase claiming extra money must be wired to cover unexpected "customs tariffs" before the item ships .

Rental & Housing Fraud: Scammers lift photos of real Central Illinois properties to post fake online rental listings, or circulate bogus Section 8 housing waitlist flyers on Facebook to harvest personal data from college students and families .
Never pay over the phone: Legitimate government agencies, courts, and police departments will never demand immediate payment via gift cards, Bitcoin, or phone transfers .
Do not click links in texts: Unsolicited SMS alerts from services like Netflix, delivery couriers, or state offices should be ignored or verified independently through official websites.
Verify directly: If you receive a worrisome call claiming to be from a local sheriff or agency, hang up and call the official department number listed on their verified municipal website.

text_blocks.snippet: If you want to report a specific incident or need information on a different type of fraud, tell me what kind of suspicious message or call you received so I can provide more tailored safety steps.
